Your call. With ~80% of the account in cash and the Buffett Indicator at an all-time extreme, sitting on dry powder until SPXC reconciles and a real catalyst shows up isn't a cost.

🔄 Rotation Suggestions

None. One open position (GOOG, within its bracket), no dead money, no TP hit. The SPXC item above is a bookkeeping sync, not a rotation. Best move today is no move.

📚 Today you learned

Sell-the-News

A catalyst can resolve exactly as expected and the stock still drops — because the price already moved to reflect the expected outcome before the event, and "expected" is what gets sold. You've lived this twice already: CELC got FDA-approved three days early and still fell from $111 to your $91.63 exit because the commercial launch was delayed and the approval was already priced in. VERA got approved Jul 7 and immediately drifted below $38 support into your stop — same mechanic, bigger size (−$33.28). The tell is price action in the hours after the news: if a "good" headline doesn't hold its initial pop, the move was already in the price. Going into TSM (Oct 15) and MSFT (~Oct 27), this is why the options-implied move (taught Day 17) matters more than the headline beat/miss — the question is never "did they beat," it's "did they beat by more than what was already priced in."

Also today: Earnings whisper numbers (Day 16) — the buyside's unofficial, usually-higher expectation that actually moves the stock, as distinct from the published sellside consensus.
